correctness.rationale: Universality and homogeneity turn the labelled extensions into precisely the injective ordered types disjoint from the named star. Given the hub-and-tuple core, the one-leaf triangle tests are sufficient: with two old leaves their distance is 2, between the difference and sum of any two entries in {1,2,3}. Thus the leaf choices are independent, also for n=0; the hub vector itself is admissible. A non-2 hub entry bounds the base by 2·3^(k−1), and with hub entries all 2 a length-1 tuple edge forbids two of nine pairs. A length-3 edge forbids just the pair (1,1). Two length-3 edges have 22 assignments on three coordinates if incident, and 64 on four if disjoint, with 64<3·22. For any additional length-3 edge, putting 1 exactly on its endpoints and 2 elsewhere exhibits a newly forbidden assignment. These bounds give the unique unrestricted core, the single length-3 edge cores and the two incident length-3 edge cores, all admissible since their distances are 2 and 3. Their counts are 1, C(k,2), and 3C(k,3). Integer bases give the stated remainder, and (8/9)^2<22/27 gives the reciprocal probability estimate. Direct triangle counting for k=1,2 gives the small spectra; the recorded finite checks are corroboration, not the basis of the all-k proof.
residual_risks: The executable's recorded checks only cover the indicated finite ranges; no executable or formal proof for all arities is claimed.
